description:

The power industry has largely solved the question of whether critical power assets should be connected. UPS systems, PDUs, and power management platforms are now routinely integrated with cloud services, remote support, and operational analytics. The harder question is whether these assets are deployed in a way that justifies the trust being placed in them. Even when products are Secure by Design and Secure by Default, commissioning and integration decisions often determine the real cybersecurity outcome. Yet these activities are frequently led by teams focused on operational performance and uptime rather than cyber risk. This session examines why commissioning may be the most important security event in a power asset's lifecycle and outlines practical approaches for establishing security from day one through secure commissioning, secure-by-deployment principles, and lifecycle risk management.

Join our ICS/OT Cybersecurity star Mike Holcomb and Power specialist Saltanat Mashirova for this in-depth talk, and be sure to bring your questions for her!

name: The Platform Clinic in the age of AI: Fix what's not working, identify new inve…
description:
Join Ajay Chankramath and Mallory Haigh for the first Platform Clinic of our virtual series, a working session on what's actually breaking on platforms in the age of AI. Bring a real problem. Leave with a clear read on where your platform gaps sit across adoption, value measurement, and AI readiness, plus practical next steps you can act on straight away.

The first in our virtual Platform Clinic series, a continuation of the in-person clinics run at PlatformCon London and NYC.
Most platform teams now have something in production, but they're facing patchy adoption, unclear ROI, or an AI mandate they're not confident the platform can support. This session works through those problems in the open, with peers facing the same thing.
We'll run three guided breakouts: what your team has built that nobody uses and why, how you'd prove platform ROI if your CTO asked tomorrow (with AI in the mix), and what breaks first when an AI mandate scales past the pilot. For platform leads, VPs and Directors of Engineering, and CTOs. Off the record, no recording, live discussion throughout.

Speaker: Ajay Chankramath
CTO, Platform Engineering Consulting
Ajay Chankramath is CTO at Platform Engineering Consulting (PEC), where he leads client engagements as one of the practitioners who defined the discipline. His career spans nearly four decades as an engineer, architect, and engineering leader across platform engineering, developer experience, cloud, FinOps, and SRE, including roles as Head of Platform Engineering at Thoughtworks, CTO at Brillio and CEO at Platformetrics. He has senior leadership experience in FinTech, Cloud SaaS, and Semiconductor industries.

At PEC, his current focus includes agentic AI for platform engineering and domain-driven platform engineering. He is co-author of *Effective Platform Engineering* (Manning) and *Domain-Driven Platform Engineering* (Springer), and author of the *Platform Engineer's Handbook* (Packt). He's a regular keynote speaker at platform engineering conferences like PlatformCon and an educator at Platform Engineering University, O'Reilly, Pearson, and Packt.

Speaker: Mallory Haigh
Mallory Haigh is Head of Platform Education and Advocacy at Platform Engineering Consulting (PEC), where she creates and teaches the Platform Engineering University certification tracks (Practitioner, Leader, Professional, and AI in PE). She brings 17+ years of experience as a full-stack engineer, consultant, and developer advocate, with a background in anthropology that shapes her focus on the intersection of humans and technology. Over the past 5+ years, she's partnered with engineering leadership at enterprise organizations to drive platform adoption, having worked hands-on across dozens of platforms of varying scale.

name: Search Is a Content Problem
description:
Search Is a Content Problem: How Metadata, IA, and Governance Shape Discoverability

**About the talk:**

If you've heard users say they feel that your "search is broken" or that "they can't find anything", they're often pointing to a content problem. Search depends on clear titles, useful metadata, and strong content structure. When those pieces are weak, search results can't help your users. In this session, we’ll look at how to find and fix these problems. Lucy will share how audits, metadata reviews, and simple content changes can improve what users see in search. We’ll also look at how to prevent the same problems from coming back by setting clear content rules and standards.

**This will be a hands-on session in Mural.** You are invited to listen and participate at the level you're comfortable with.

**About Lucy:**
Lucy is a Senior Digital Strategist focused on making digital content easier to navigate and use. Her work has included just about every sort of of content strategy task. From complex site audits, microcopy writing, and content modeling. All the way to engaging stakeholders directly to promote better user experiences. She has over two decades of experience in human-centered design, which has served her well in all of her work. She focuses on building relationships with clients to build trust. Which helps bring empathy for all users into the room when decisions get made.

name: Thinking in Platforms: Thrive in the agentic era
description:
Ahead of the August 2026 launch of Thinking in Platforms, join authors Kaspar von Grünberg and Luca Galante for a live session on platform engineering as the operating model for the AI era. See how leading organizations turn recurring knowledge work into reliable production systems, and why a strong platform is the real prerequisite for AI-driven productivity.

The first in a pre-launch webinar series for Thinking in Platforms, the new book by Kaspar von Grünberg and Luca Galante (out August 2026).
Platform engineering started in software but is becoming a discipline for redesigning how organizations work. The authors unpack their core thesis: the biggest gains come from turning recurring knowledge work into scalable production systems, not from working harder or adding AI on top.
Expect an early look at the Paths to Outcome model and the playbook behind it, plus why clear interfaces and clean data are what let AI actually deliver. For leaders, builders, and operators, with live Q&A to follow.

Speaker: Luca Galante

Speaker: Kaspar von Grünberg

name: Context-aware Vibe Coding for Platform Engineering
description:
Vibe coding lets platform engineers build agents and platform enhancements in plain language to eliminate toil across the SDLC. But moving from POC to production is where teams get stuck: the hard part isn't the prompt, it's the context - so agents know your stack, teams, dependencies, and act within your policies. This hands-on session shows how to reliably build agents for common SDLC use cases.

You’ll learn:
- How to vibe-code on top of real-time context - so agents run in production, not as templates
- Core AI Skills around SRE, DevOps, and security needed to build solutions that work for platform engineers
- Concrete tips and design considerations for building production-grade SDLC agents: scoping, loops, human-in-the-loop, and more.
- How to let other teams contribute agents without making platform engineers the bottleneck - while keeping visibility and control
- Demo: vibe-coding 3 use cases you can run today: governing AI-generated PRs, tracking AI impact, wiring new integrations to your stack.

Speaker: Roi Fine
Growth Product Manager @ Port
Roi Fine is a Growth Product Manager at Port, focused on helping platform engineers onboard and succeed with the platform. He works at the intersection of product, data, and go-to-market, spending much of his time talking with customers and turning their needs into product direction. His current focus is helping teams build their agentic platform for the SDLC with Port. Outside of work, you can find him hiking or at his fiction book club.

Speaker: John Crowley
Technical PMM @ Port
John Crowley is a Technical Product Marketing Manager at Port, supporting the Agent Management solution. With a background in product management and strategy, he enjoys solving problems for technical users. Before joining Port, John worked on teams building cybersecurity and defense software products.

name: VeltoraCore - The Optimization Layer for Fragmented Markets
description:
Join us for a discussion about the new VeltoraCore lab that is building a pair-coin, system-agnostic optimization engine that jointly coordinates user execution and LP participation in a single feasibility framework. A lightweight Proof-of-Optimization (PoO) mechanism cryptographically commits optimized batch outcomes to external system states, enabling verifiable cross-system settlement. Simulations on the ETH–USD pair show superior retained execution and materially lower user fees relative to benchmarks, while delivering liquidity-provider returns higher with reduced volatility.

This is a great opportunity to talk to the developers about what they're building and to learn how to get involved if this sounds interesting.

More about the VeltoraCore lab is at: [https://github.com/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/veltoracore](https://github.com/LF-Decentralized-Trust-labs/veltoracore)
